datasets.name: Lens-800M
datasets.description: The 800-million-pair training corpus named in the Microsoft Lens report, featuring long GPT-4.1-generated captions averaging about 109 words.

access.notes: The paper names and characterizes the corpus but does not publish a dataset download.

scale.notes: Scale is reported by the Lens authors.

license.media: Not disclosed
license.notes: The training corpus is described in the paper but its sources and terms are not disclosed.

known_limitations: Source composition, filtering thresholds, rights, and release plan are undisclosed.
GPT-4.1-generated captions can propagate model-specific biases or hallucinations.

processing.notes: Preserve caption-model version and original text if reproducing this strategy.

datasets.name: VGGSound-Omni
datasets.organization: Tsinghua University, Monash University, and Shengshu AI
datasets.description: A unified audio-generation benchmark derived from the VGGSound test set with human-verified dense captions for more than 14,000 videos and a dedicated 1,613-item off-screen track spanning natural events and synthetic music.

access.notes: The benchmark is distributed with SoundAtlas after acceptance of the repository access terms.

scale.notes: The primary track covers 14,000+ VGGSound test videos; the off-screen track contains 1,613 items.

license.media: Source-dependent VGGSound, YouTube, and MusicCaps terms
license.notes: The benchmark repository is CC-BY-NC-4.0, while the underlying videos and mixed music retain source-platform and source-dataset conditions.

known_limitations: The benchmark is constructed by the Omni2Sound authors and can share their captioning-style biases.
Human review is targeted through an AI-assisted mismatch audit rather than described as uniform double annotation.
Part of the off-screen track is synthetically mixed and may not match natural background-music distributions.

processing.notes: Preserve primary versus off-screen track, natural versus synthetic origin, modality labels, and source media ID.

datasets.name: SoundAtlas
datasets.organization: Tsinghua University, Monash University, and Shengshu AI
datasets.description: A roughly 470-thousand-pair audio-caption corpus derived from AudioSet and VGGSound with temporally grounded descriptions of audible and visual context.

access.notes: Access requires accepting the repository terms and sharing contact information.

scale.notes: The project and paper consistently describe SoundAtlas as about 470K pairs.

license.media: Source-dependent AudioSet and VGGSound media terms
license.notes: The Hugging Face repository applies CC-BY-NC-4.0 to the release, while the underlying media remains subject to its original source and platform terms.

known_limitations: Source media availability and rights can change independently of the released annotations.
Model-generated captions can retain hallucinations despite multimodal consistency filtering.
The two upstream collections have different collection processes and label distributions.

processing.notes: Retain source identifiers, captioning-agent versions, alignment scores, and media-fetch status.

datasets.name: AudioCaps 2.0
datasets.description: The second AudioCaps release, containing 98,606 human-written caption rows grounded in ten-second AudioSet and YouTube segments, roughly doubling the original audio-caption collection.

access.notes: Caption CSV files are public, while raw video and audio access requires submitting the maintainer form.

scale.notes: The official v2.0 split counts are 91,256 train, 2,475 validation, and 4,875 test caption rows.

license.metadata: Academic use only; no standalone SPDX dataset license stated
license.media: AudioSet and YouTube source terms; raw media supplied by request
license.notes: The official repository permits the code and dataset for academic purposes only; its MIT repository license must not be treated as a media license.

known_limitations: The 98,606 count is caption rows and is not documented as a unique-clip count.
AudioCaps 2.0 is a 2025 data update not evaluated in the original 2019 paper.
YouTube availability changes over time, so a later fetch can contain fewer usable clips.

processing.notes: Preserve YouTube ID, start offset, split, caption row ID, fetch time, and media hash.

datasets.name: FineVideo
datasets.description: A collection of Creative Commons YouTube videos with rich descriptions, scene-level structure, transcripts, and question-answer annotations.

access.notes: Users must accept dataset terms before accessing the repository.

scale.notes: The maintainers report over 43K videos spanning about 3.4K hours.

license.media: Per-video Creative Commons terms
license.notes: Users must preserve attribution and provenance, follow current usable versions and removals, and include the dataset terms when sharing access.

known_limitations: Long-form videos are not equivalent to generation-ready short clips.
The usable version can change when validated removal requests are processed.

processing.notes: Use scene annotations to derive clips and retain attribution per source video.

datasets.name: Re-LAION-5B
datasets.description: A safety-revised release of LAION-5B metadata intended to remove known harmful links while preserving a reproducible web-scale image-text index.

access.notes: LAION distributes metadata rather than the underlying image files.

scale.notes: Derived from the 5.85B-pair LAION-5B index after safety revisions.

license.media: Source-dependent and not distributed by LAION
license.notes: Metadata licensing does not grant copyright or other rights to images resolved from third-party URLs. Apply takedowns and current safety lists.

known_limitations: Web metadata can be noisy, biased, unsafe, or stale.
The reconstructed media corpus changes as source URLs disappear.

processing.notes: Re-check hashes, safety signals, access results, and rights at ingestion time.

datasets.name: OpenVid-1M
datasets.description: A curated collection of one million high-quality video clips with expressive captions, including a large high-definition subset for video generation.

access.notes: Videos, CSV metadata, and split archives are hosted on Hugging Face.

scale.notes: The project reports about 1M clips, including 433K clips at 1080p.

license.media: Source-dependent with research and non-commercial restrictions stated
license.notes: The dataset card asks users to follow licenses of upstream video datasets and states a research and non-commercial intent despite the CC-BY label.

known_limitations: Upstream datasets have different or unknown media terms.
Curated aesthetic distributions may narrow content diversity.

processing.notes: Validate archives, normalize codecs, and preserve upstream dataset provenance.

datasets.name: Panda-70M
datasets.description: A large video-caption corpus produced by splitting source videos into semantically consistent clips and captioning them with multiple teachers.

access.notes: CSV metadata and download tooling are provided for source videos.

scale.notes: Statistics refer to the full training split reported by the project.

license.media: Source-dependent
license.notes: The maintainers require users to follow the related license of publicly sourced video samples; availability is primarily metadata plus tooling.

known_limitations: Download success and the resulting corpus vary with source availability.
Machine captions and scores can propagate teacher-model biases.

processing.notes: Retain source video IDs and clip timestamps through download and sharding.

datasets.name: Pick-a-Pic v2
datasets.organization: Tel Aviv University and Meta AI
datasets.description: An open collection of real user choices between pairs of text-to-image model outputs, with prompts and preference labels for alignment research.

access.notes: The canonical Hugging Face repository currently requires authenticated access.

scale.notes: The v2 release is described as containing more than one million examples.

license.media: Model-output and source-term dependent
license.notes: Confirm the current dataset card and the terms of image-generating models; a dataset license may not resolve every right in generated outputs.

known_limitations: Online user preferences are self-selected and not demographically representative.
Repeated prompts, users, and model versions can create leakage or dependence.

processing.notes: Split by prompt and user provenance where possible to reduce evaluation leakage.

datasets.name: InternVid
datasets.description: A web-scale video-text corpus built from millions of source videos and segmented into captioned clips for multimodal understanding and generation.

access.notes: Public releases include metadata and filtered subsets such as InternVid-10M-FLT.

scale.notes: Paper-level full-corpus statistics; accessible subsets may be much smaller.

license.media: Source-dependent
license.notes: The Apache-2.0 repository license covers code, not necessarily third-party web videos. Review the dataset card and each intended media use.

known_limitations: Full paper scale and currently downloadable subsets are not equivalent.
Web video availability, safety, and rights can change over time.

processing.notes: Record subset name and version before comparing results or publishing counts.

datasets.name: Objaverse-XL
datasets.description: A web-scale collection of more than ten million deduplicated 3D objects from multiple public sources, designed to support 3D foundation models and large multiview-rendering pipelines.

access.notes: Official tooling resolves source assets; some subsets, notably Polycam, require separate access.

scale.notes: The project reports over 10 million 3D objects rather than a fixed frozen count.

license.media: Per-object source license
license.notes: Dataset metadata is ODC-By-1.0, while each object retains its source license; the Polycam contribution is explicitly non-commercial and separately gated.

known_limitations: Asset formats, geometry quality, topology, textures, and metadata vary substantially by source.
Source objects may disappear or change after a metadata snapshot is published.
Dataset-level openness does not override non-commercial or custom per-object licenses.

processing.notes: Snapshot metadata first, validate object decodes, deduplicate by UID and content, and retain per-object terms.

datasets.name: JourneyDB
datasets.organization: CUHK MMLab and Shanghai AI Laboratory
datasets.description: A dataset of high-resolution Midjourney-generated images paired with prompts, captions, and visual question answering annotations.

access.notes: Access follows the distribution and request flow linked by the project.

scale.notes: The project page reports 4,429,295 generated images.

license.media: Generated-media terms require review
license.notes: Images originate from Midjourney generations and user prompts; review the current dataset agreement and platform terms for the intended use.

known_limitations: The corpus reflects the behavior and user distribution of a closed generator.
Generated-image provenance does not by itself establish unrestricted reuse.

processing.notes: Preserve prompt, caption, VQA, and source identifiers as separate fields.

datasets.name: Cap3D
datasets.description: A large 3D-text release with automated captions for Objaverse and Objaverse-XL objects plus point clouds, multi-view renders, camera metadata, depth, alpha masks, and Shap-E latents for substantial subsets.

access.notes: Captions and derived assets are published through Hugging Face and the official repository.

scale.notes: The current full caption CSV reports 785,150 Objaverse objects and the remainder from Objaverse-XL.

license.media: Per-object source license
license.notes: Cap3D licenses its captions and derived release under ODC-By-1.0, but users must also comply with the license attached to each source 3D object.

known_limitations: Individual source objects can prohibit commercial use or impose additional conditions.
Automated captions can omit fine geometry or infer attributes that are not visible from all views.
Not every object has every derived representation in the published asset archives.

processing.notes: Join all derived files by object UID and preserve the original object license beside every sample.

datasets.name: DataComp-1B
datasets.description: A filtered billion-scale image-text subset released with the DataComp benchmark for studying data selection under fixed training settings.

access.notes: Metadata and tooling are provided; media is fetched from source URLs.

scale.notes: The project uses DataComp-1B as the nominal name for its best xlarge subset.

license.metadata: See DataComp repository and dataset documentation
license.media: Source-dependent
license.notes: The repository license does not grant rights to media downloaded from third-party URLs; evaluate the original assets and terms separately.

known_limitations: URL decay changes the retrievable corpus over time.
Web-scale content requires independent safety and rights review.

processing.notes: Official tooling downloads URL-backed samples into WebDataset shards.

datasets.name: WavCaps
datasets.organization: Centre for Vision, Speech and Signal Processing, University of Surrey
datasets.description: A 403,050-pair weakly labelled audio-caption corpus assembled from FreeSound, BBC Sound Effects, SoundBible, and the strongly labelled AudioSet subset, with noisy source descriptions filtered and rewritten using ChatGPT.

access.notes: JSON metadata and FLAC archives are hosted on Hugging Face without an account gate.

scale.notes: The official card reports 403,050 clips averaging 67.59 seconds, or about 7.6K hours.

license.media: Academic-use-only project terms plus per-source FreeSound, BBC, SoundBible, and AudioSet terms
license.notes: The Hugging Face metadata carries a CC-BY-4.0 label, but the official card also restricts WavCaps audio to academic research and requires source-level attribution; the stricter documented boundary is recorded here.

known_limitations: ChatGPT-generated captions can normalize away useful detail or introduce unsupported events.
Audio duration, recording quality, and description style vary substantially across the four sources.
Dataset-level metadata and narrative usage terms are not internally consistent about licensing.

processing.notes: Keep raw and transformed descriptions, source license, captioning version, duration, and content hash.

datasets.name: COYO-700M
datasets.description: A large collection of image and text metadata pairs gathered from web pages, with source URLs and filtering signals for multimodal pretraining.

access.notes: The hosted dataset primarily provides metadata and source image URLs.

scale.notes: The public project describes the collection at 700M scale.

license.media: Source-dependent
license.notes: CC-BY-4.0 covers the COYO dataset release; underlying images remain subject to rights and terms associated with their original sources.

known_limitations: Source URLs can expire or return changed content.
Web alt-text is not a consistently descriptive training caption.

processing.notes: Download with retries and preserve source provenance and failure reasons.

datasets.name: WebVid-10M
datasets.description: A historically influential collection of captioned short stock-footage videos whose original URL and caption distribution has been withdrawn.

access.notes: The maintainer states that the dataset is no longer distributed.

scale.notes: The project describes a corpus at roughly ten million video-text pairs.

license.media: Third-party stock footage
license.notes: The original distributor withdrew URLs and captions after a cease-and-desist; the repository mentions only internal non-commercial use of existing copies.

known_limitations: The canonical dataset cannot currently be obtained from the maintainer.
Stock-site captions can include subjective or non-visual language.

processing.notes: Kept as historical context; do not treat mirrors as authoritative releases.

datasets.name: Clotho 2.1
datasets.description: Version 2.1 of the curated audio-captioning dataset, with 6,974 Freesound excerpts and five human-written captions per sample, for 34,870 captions.

access.notes: Audio archives, caption CSV files, metadata, and checksums are directly hosted on Zenodo.

scale.notes: Each sample is 15 to 30 seconds long and has five captions.

license.metadata: Per-file Freesound licenses recorded in the metadata CSV files
license.media: Mostly Creative Commons with attribution; exact license is attached to each audio file
license.notes: The captions use Tampere University's mainly attribution and non-commercial license, while every Freesound excerpt retains its own recorded license.

known_limitations: Caption wording was constrained to avoid named entities, speech transcription, and split-specific singleton words.
Per-file media terms are not replaced by the dataset-level caption license.
Omni2Sound names Clotho without identifying which release was used.

processing.notes: Preserve the split, all five captions, Freesound URL, uploader, file license, and archive checksum.

datasets.name: FSD50K
datasets.organization: Music Technology Group, Universitat Pompeu Fabra
datasets.description: An open collection of 51,197 human-labelled Freesound clips totalling 108.3 hours, organized into 200 AudioSet-derived sound-event classes with raw audio, metadata, and per-file licenses.

access.notes: Raw development and evaluation audio, labels, metadata, documentation, and checksums are hosted on Zenodo.

scale.notes: The development split has 40,966 clips and the evaluation split 10,231 clips.

license.media: Per-clip CC0, CC-BY, CC-BY-NC, or CC Sampling+ license
license.notes: The dataset-level CC BY license does not erase clip-level restrictions; 6,041 clips carry CC-BY-NC and 1,777 carry CC Sampling+ terms.

known_limitations: Development labels can be correct but incomplete, unlike the exhaustively labelled evaluation set.
Class and uploader distributions are imbalanced.
Commercial reuse requires filtering or separately clearing clips with restrictive licenses.

processing.notes: Preserve Freesound ID, uploader, clip-level license, label provenance, split, waveform hash, and archive checksum.

datasets.name: VGGSound
datasets.organization: Visual Geometry Group, University of Oxford
datasets.description: An automatically curated audiovisual sound-event dataset with more than 210,000 ten-second YouTube videos across 310 classes, selected for visible and audible source correspondence.

access.notes: The official repository distributes YouTube IDs, offsets, labels, and splits rather than a durable media archive.

scale.notes: The paper reports more than 210K ten-second videos; current retrievable media can be substantially smaller.

license.media: Copyright remains with the original video owners
license.notes: The repository permits commercial and research use under CC BY 4.0 while explicitly retaining original-owner copyright for the source videos.

known_limitations: Automated visual and audio verification can retain label noise and miss off-screen sources.
YouTube deletions make the effective corpus size dependent on fetch date.
The paper, repository, and later derivatives use slightly different class and sample counts.

processing.notes: Preserve release CSV, YouTube ID, offset, label, split, fetch time, availability result, and media hash.

datasets.name: FMA
datasets.description: A music-analysis dataset with 106,574 Creative Commons-licensed tracks, 343 days of audio, hierarchical genre labels, metadata, free-form text, and precomputed acoustic features.

access.notes: The official repository links full, large, medium, and small audio archives plus metadata and features.

scale.notes: The paper reports 917 GiB and 343 days of audio from 16,341 artists and 14,854 albums.

license.metadata: Dataset code is MIT; metadata and features carry their documented component terms
license.media: Creative Commons license recorded per track
license.notes: Tracks that prohibited redistribution were removed during curation, but retained tracks still use differing Creative Commons terms, including licenses that can restrict commercial reuse or require attribution.

known_limitations: Genre and metadata distributions are highly imbalanced and retain real-world outliers.
The four official subsets differ in duration and genre balance.
Every training export must retain the original per-track license and attribution fields.

processing.notes: Preserve FMA track ID, subset, full metadata, per-track license, original duration, and audio hash.

datasets.name: AudioSet
datasets.description: A large human-labelled sound-event corpus of 2,084,320 ten-second YouTube segments spanning 527 active labels, distributed as URL annotations and precomputed audio features rather than raw waveforms.

access.notes: Google hosts segment CSV files and VGGish features; it does not distribute the source YouTube audio.

scale.notes: The official explorer reports about 5.8K hours across 2,084,320 ten-second segments.

license.media: Raw YouTube audio is not distributed and remains subject to source-platform and uploader rights
license.notes: Google's Creative Commons terms cover the released dataset artifacts, not a separately redistributable archive of the underlying YouTube media.

known_limitations: Most labels are weak at the ten-second segment level and can be incomplete.
Source videos disappear or change, making later raw-audio fetches smaller and non-reproducible.
The official raw-audio distribution is unavailable; model reports often do not state the fetch snapshot.

processing.notes: Preserve YouTube ID, offsets, ontology version, split, fetch timestamp, availability result, and media hash.

datasets.name: Million Song Dataset
datasets.organization: The Echo Nest and LabROSA, Columbia University
datasets.description: A 280 GB collection of metadata and derived audio-analysis features for one million popular music tracks, with linked community subsets but no original or listenable audio in the official distribution.

access.notes: The stable official repository documents the project, but the legacy distribution paths are no longer reliable and never included raw audio.

scale.notes: Each HDF5 item represents one track and contains Echo Nest metadata and audio-analysis features.

license.metadata: Mixed Echo Nest API terms, public-domain fields, and linked-dataset licenses
license.media: No raw audio is included in the official dataset
license.notes: Echo Nest terms govern core features; MusicBrainz and linked subsets have separate terms, including public-domain and non-commercial components.

known_limitations: The released representation is lossy analysis data and cannot substitute for training on waveforms.
The corpus contains 944 duplicate tracks representing songs already present in the database.
Omni2Sound does not explain whether it used official MSD features or separately sourced audio previews.

processing.notes: Preserve track and song IDs, feature schema, source subset, linked-dataset license, and conversion provenance.

datasets.name: VGGSound-Omni
datasets.notes: Released with the benchmark repository for unified T2A, V2A, VT2A, and off-screen audio evaluation.

stages.name: pretraining
stages.strategy: Pretrain text-to-audio generation across eight named public audio and music collections before introducing visual conditioning.

stages.name: fine-tuning
stages.strategy: Interleave text-, video-, and video-text-conditioned audio generation on about 470K SoundAtlas pairs to bridge semantic and temporal controls.

stages.name: fine-tuning
stages.strategy: Add synthesized off-screen sound cases and drop text conditioning during a final robustness stage so visual control remains useful when captions are missing.

strategy_summary: Start with broad text-to-audio pretraining, then introduce aligned video and dense captions instead of training every condition from scratch.
Build SoundAtlas with audiovisual routing, agentic captioning, and CLAP plus audiovisual-text consistency filters.
Use a final off-screen-sound and text-dropout stage to reduce dependence on visible sound sources or complete prompts.

architecture.notes: Unified consumer-oriented video model with bilingual text conditioning and super-resolution.

stages.name: pretraining
stages.strategy: Progressively pretrain with curated image and video data across multiple resolutions and durations.

stages.name: fine-tuning
stages.strategy: Apply progressive post-training and glyph-aware bilingual conditioning for Chinese and English prompt fidelity.

strategy_summary: Combine curated images and videos so spatial quality and motion can scale together.
Use progressive pretraining and post-training across durations and resolutions.
Add glyph-aware bilingual text conditioning for text-rich prompts.
